name: Fenrir Thermal-Arc Parka
description:
A mid-length parka designed for GLMZ's brutal lake winters, manufactured by Fenrir — a Scandinavian-heritage brand that opened a Great Lakes production facility in 2171. The outer shell is a tightly woven ripstop nylon in matte black, navy, or a deep forest green. The interior uses a graphene-filament heating mesh powered by a thin flexible battery pack sewn into the left side panel — a USB-C style connector at the hem lets you charge from any standard port. Three heat settings, controlled by a simple push-button tab at the cuff. No app, no BCI sync, no cloud. Just warm.

The parka is sold in Tier 2 and Tier 3 retail channels and is considered one of the more honest pieces of heated apparel on the market — the tech is minimal, the construction is sound, and the battery lasts a full work shift at medium setting. Hood is furred with synthetic pile and detaches. Deep hand-warmer pockets. This is the parka you see on transit platforms and construction sites in January.
functionality: Integrated graphene heating mesh with three heat settings. Battery powers 8 hours on low, 4 hours on high. Charges via standard port at hem. No wireless connectivity.
what_it_says: You live in a cold city and you've made a sensible decision about it. The heated lining is a practical luxury, not a status one.
story_hooks: A batch of Fenrir parkas from a 2198 production run had a battery cell defect that causes intermittent overheating at the left side panel — not enough to catch fire, but enough to leave a burn mark on skin. Fenrir issued a quiet recall that many buyers never heard about.

The graphene mesh in the parka operates on a frequency that interferes with a specific older-model BCI handshake protocol — wearers with that implant generation sometimes experience brief signal dropout in high-cold situations. Nobody has formally connected these two facts yet.

A Shelf community organizer has been buying Fenrir parkas wholesale through a Tier 3 intermediary and distributing them to unhoused residents. Someone at Fenrir's distribution division has noticed the unusual bulk orders and flagged them.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian mid-length parka with a clean, no-nonsense silhouette. The matte ripstop shell absorbs light, creating a flat, industrial aesthetic. Hood sits high and structured with synthetic fur trim. Visible cuff controls and battery pack outline create subtle tech signatures without ostentatious branding. Reads as durable streetwear rather than fashion statement.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso with subtle tapering at the waist; room for layering without excess bulk. Sleeves cut straight and honest. Hem falls mid-thigh. Designed for movement and functionality over aesthetic tailoring.
physical_description.primary_material: Ripstop nylon outer shell (tightly woven, matte finish); synthetic pile fur hood lining; internal graphene-filament heating mesh; flexible battery polymer casing
physical_description.texture: Outer shell is smooth and slightly stiff with a faint grid texture from ripstop weave. Synthetic fur is uniformly dense and plush. Interior mesh has a subtle crinkle. Battery pack edge is barely perceptible through fabric.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte black as dominant option, with navy and deep forest green variants. All desaturated and muted. Minimal contrast except for dark gray battery connector at hem.
physical_description.closures: Full-length two-way YKK-style zipper with storm flap. Detachable hood secured via anchor points and tension snaps. Cuff adjustment via friction-fit velcro strap.
distinctive_features: Push-button heat control tab at left cuff (three settings, mechanical, no electronics)
USB-C charging connector at hem with subtle protective flap
Deep hand-warmer pockets with internal mesh lining
Left side panel houses thin flexible battery pack (barely visible seam)
Reinforced ripstop at high-stress points (shoulders, elbows, hem)
No visible branding except small woven Fenrir label at interior collar
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2–3 bridge: affordable luxury tech without conspicuous consumption. Built for people who work in cold environments and expect gear to just work.
physical_description.cultural_context: Transit workers, construction crews, warehouse staff, night-shift engineers, medical field responders. The choice of someone who values reliability over status. Signals Scandinavian manufacturing ethos and skepticism of cloud-dependent gadgetry.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and practical. Minor scuffs on the ripstop from use. Fur hood slightly compressed from handling. Battery connector shows wear patterns from repeated charging. Otherwise structurally sound; improves with age.

Close-up detail shot of the left cuff shows the mechanical heat control button; another angle reveals the USB-C charging port at the hem glowing faintly.
